chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasem, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Sa'id ibn al-Walid, who said: We entered with Aban ibn Taghlib to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
That I feed one Muslim till he is satisfied is more beloved to me than feeding a horizon of people. I said: How much is a horizon? He said: A hundred thousand.

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: More beloved to me, indicating personal preference and spiritual value
key_terms.أَفُقًا: A horizon, used metaphorically to denote a vast multitude or crowd of people
key_terms.يَشْبَعَ: To be satisfied or full, referring to the state of being completely fed

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred amount of charity according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the quantitative scale of charity and its qualitative impact, asserting that fully satisfying one person is superior to feeding a vast multitude who may remain partially satisfied. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikmal* (completeness) and the depth of benefit in individual acts of kindness over mere numerical volume. The definition of 'a horizon' (*afuq*) as 100,000 people serves to illustrate the immense scale required to outweigh the spiritual merit of perfecting the nourishment of a single individual.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasem, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, from Hasan bin Ali bin Yusuf, from Saif bin ‘Umayra, from Sa’eed bin Waleed, that he said: We entered with Aban bin Taghlib into the place of Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, and Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:
Verily, that I feed one Muslim till he is satisfied is more beloved to me than feeding a horizon of people. I said: How much is a horizon? He said: A hundred thousand.
